Introduction
Spatial Training Room is an automated data factory that converts a 3D indoor reconstruction (Gaussian Splatting scene) + per-object AABB annotations + room polygon maps into Active Perception Learning (APL) training samples. Each sample is a 4D question: (init_view, expert_action_sequence, target_view, question, answer). The initial viewpoint is deliberately selected so the question is unanswerable— the agent must actively navigate (pan, tilt, translate) to gather sufficient visual evidence before answering. The 19 active task templates cover spatial reasoning across occlusion, cross-room, counting, configuration, distance, and navigability.
System Pipeline
# ── Input ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── scene/ 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction + AABB labels + room polygons templates/p0/*.yaml task "skeletons" — evidence slots, QA format, scoring rules ↓ template_active_generator.py Instantiate skeleton with scene objects Select init view # MUST be unanswerable (tier2_override fix applied) Expert BFS search # shortest path to full slot coverage ↓ out/fixed_v6/*.jsonl one line = one task with full expert trajectory ↓ render_real_tasks.py render trajectory frames via Gaussian Splatting (CPU splat)
Key Fix: tier2_override Init-View Selection
🔧 template_active_generator.py — strict submit-time init check
Slots with tier2_override (e.g. target must be fully invisible at init) previously used the raw predicate fraction for the init-view rejection test, allowing some tier2 slots to pass even when slot_satisfied(..., submit_only=True) would reject them. The fix branches on s.tier2_override and calls slot_satisfied() with submit_only=True for tier2 slots, so init views that are too informative are correctly rejected.

Result: init answerability drops to 0 / 25 = 0.0% on the probe regression.
